page0.text: I have to decide what I'm going to do next.

page1.text:
I chose to keep fighting.
Zouken Matou and Assassin...
The black Shadow roaming the town...
Masters fighting each other over the Holy Grail...
I decided I'd stop it all, even if I lost Saber.
This is not time to worry about appearances.
I need Tohsaka's help if I want to prevent any further victims.

page2.text:
"Tohsaka.
I've lost Saber and my Command Spells, so I'm not a Master anymore, right?"

page3.text: "...Yeah. I forgot that important detail. You're not a Master anymore. You don't need to involve yourself with the Holy Grail War, and you're less likely to be targeted by the other Masters now."

page4.text:
"Right. I wanted the Grail because Saber said she needed it. Now that she's gone, I'm not interested in it anymore."
"Okay. So you're going to stop fighting?"

page5.text:
Tohsaka's eyes are stoic.
She asks me the question as a Master, evenly and without letting her own emotions cloud it.

page6.text:
...
It's a warning, not a question.
This is my last chance.
She's giving me fair warning that it isn't too late to turn back.

page7.text:
"...No."
But my answer was decided long ago.
I'm going to remember how considerate she was for asking me.

page8.text:
"Of course not. I won't forfeit this war, even if I'm not a Master. I decided I'd fight to put a stop to it."
"All right. Then we can continue our relationship.
We're mutual enemies, but we have a truce until we beat that 'Shadow' thing."

page9.text:
"Hm?"
Tohsaka smiles suddenly.
Her stoicness from a moment ago turns to friendliness, as if something nice just happened.
...That's fine, I guess. It's not like I'd know why.

page10.text:
"Hang on. Why are we enemies?
I'm not a Master anymore. I have no reason to compete with you."

page11.text:
"What are you talking about? You might've lost your Servant and Command Spells, but that doesn't mean you aren't Saber's Master.
You were chosen by the Holy Grail, even if it wasn't according to plan. That means you have a right to it, too. You might be neutralized for now, but you're still a contender."

page12.text: "I am? Even if I don't care about getting the Holy Grail?"

page13.text:
That depends on the situation. It's completely possible that you might get the Holy Grail and find yourself in a situation where you need its power.
People without greed are influenced by external factors precisely because they have no personal desires."

page14.text: "Hrm. You're overthinking this, Tohsaka. Even if I needed the Grail, there's no way I'd get it."

page15.text:
"It's just hypothetical, but the possibility isn't zero.
That's why I consider us enemies. It's why mages who aren't Masters anymore flee to the church for sanctuary.
Even if they've lost their Servants, they're still nuisances to the other Masters. You'd better be careful. Zouken isn't the only one gunning for you."

page16.text:
"Mrgh...I'll accept your advice."
I'm not happy about still being enemies with her.

page17.text:
"Hm? What's the complicated expression for? I said we're enemies, but things will stay the same. What's there to worry about?"
"Plenty. Because then I can't ask you for help."

page18.text:
"Huh?"
She freezes.
Tohsaka stares at me like she's just seen a ghost.

page20.text: "Because I definitely can't do this on my own. I need to defeat the other Masters to stop the war, but I don't have the power to do that."

page21.text:
"...I know it sounds pathetic, but I can't worry about appearances. Out of the few options I have left, I think this is the best one.
So I can't be enemies with you, Tohsaka.
I want you to help me, not just honor a truce."

page22.text:
"...Hold on. Have you lost your mind?"
"I'm completely sane. I'm not strong, and I might drag you down.
You don't have anything to gain by teaming up with me, and I have no way to repay you.
...Yeah. Normally, there wouldn't be any reason to form an alliance."

page23.text:
"H-hmph. So you understand that much.
As you said, equivalent exchange is a fundamental idea in magecraft. I can't help someone who has nothing to give in return, nor can I help someone who can't contribute to the team effort. You know as well as I do that it wouldn't be good for you."

page24.text: "I've been letting you consult me during our truce, but an alliance is a different story. If we're going to be friends who help each other, then there has to be something in it for both of us."

page25.text:
"Yeah. I knew that when I asked.
Help me, Tohsaka. I'll pay you back as long as I live."

page27.text:
...I know what a burden I'd be to her.
But Tohsaka's the most reliable person I know, and if she's the one who gets the Holy Grail, I can trust that nothing will go wrong.
So she's the only one I can think of helping win as a Master.

page28.text:
"Tohsaka. I'd like to hear your answer."
I meet her eyes.
"...I-it's obvious, isn't it? I'm not going to team up with someone who isn't a Master—"

page29.text:
"Tohsaka."
"I told you, even if you insist, I can't help you. To begin with—"

page30.text:
"Tohsaka."
"...It's like we're talking about a real contract, you know?"

page31.text:
There it is.
Tohsaka makes a show of looking down.
"Oh, fine! I get it! Here's my conditions, then!"
She shoots a hard gaze right back at me.

page32.text:
"What conditions?"
"My conditions for this deal!
...I'm talking about a proper contract.
If you mean what you just said, then I can think of a way to make it work."

page33.text:
"??? Tohsaka, I've been saying this whole time that I don't have anything to pay you with."
"Just listen!"
"...! O-okay, go ahead."
